newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INSTANT VIEW - Brazil's '96 $5.5 bln trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Brazil's '96 $5.5 bln trade deficit.

text.p: Following are comments from economists on Brazil's $5.539 billion record trade deficit in 1996.

ODAIR ABATE, chief economist at Lloyds Bank, Brazil: "It was a high number, considering that most of the deficit was concentrated in the second half of the year. At this pace, we will have a higher trade deficit in 1997 but we don't think it will be explosive or out of control."
Abate said the trade gap will continue to pressure Brazil's current account deficit -- expected to close 1996 at about 3.0 percent of gross domestic product.
But he said there was more than enough foreign direct investment to finance the trade gap.

Brazil's trade shortfall will grow by an average of $1 billion a month in the first quarter, Abate said. Exports will get a boost beginning in April, when Brazil begins exporting its agricultural crops, he said.

MAURO SCHNEIDER, chief economist ING Barings in Brazil: "Although the deficit was higher than expected (at the beginning of the month) ... it is not likely to have an impact on the financial markets," Schneider said, adding similar numbers were widely reported in the Brazilian press Monday.
Schneider, speaking on Reuter Financial Television, said it was unlikely the government would resort to tinkering with monetary or foreign exchange policy to reverse the worsening trade trend.
One option would be to slow the economy through credit restrictions, but there are still doubts about the level of economic activity in Brazil, Schneider said.

FLAVIO NOLASCO, economist at MA Consultores Economicos: "The 1996 figure shows a clear trend the trade deficit will be higher this year. We expect 1997's trade deficit to reach $7 billion, with exports of $52 billion and imports of $59 billion."
Nolasco also noted exports should get a boost this year because of the agricultural crop and a recent financing scheme designed to promote export growth.
